conviction_note: GameStop already put its Q2 numbers out under item 2.02 on 2026-08-31 alongside a financing, and the stock then rallied 7.2% in five sessions into a 8 September release that can largely only restate them - so the reaction distribution should be far tighter than the 4.79% median and tilted to a fade, which is why I take a third of the median and sign it down.

findings.finding: GameStop disclosed results of operations under item 2.02 twice in eight days: an 8-K accepted 2026-08-31T06:23:08Z carrying items 1.01, 2.02, 3.02, 7.01 and 9.01 - i.e. preliminary quarterly results bundled with a material agreement and an unregistered sale of equity securities - and then the 8-K accepted 2026-09-08T09:02:39Z carrying only items 2.02, 7.01 and 9.01; the 08-31 disclosure moved the stock +2.85% on 10.95m shares against a 6.20m 20-day average, and the stock then rose a further 7.2% over five sessions to $19.16, so the 9 September print inherits a bid-up tape and almost no headline surprise capacity.

findings.why_not_priced: The item codes are the whole finding and nobody aggregates them: an earnings calendar shows one date, 8 September, and an implied move sized off this company's 4.79% median reaction. What is actually happening is a pre-release, and the baseline itself only got as far as flagging the cadence as 'suspect' (8 days against a 91-day gap, history_usable 0) without resolving which of the two dates carried the news. If the market had priced the pre-release properly, the five sessions after 08-31 would not have added another 7.2% on 4.8m-11.8m share days into a release with nothing new to say.
findings.independence: Confirmed from a completely different source: the StockTwits digest fetched 2026-09-07T15:08:21Z contains a post at 2026-09-06T11:55:53Z titled 'GME Kills the VWAP early, Q2 prelim results, my trading position update & GME current Fair Value Update' (docs/41a4a7aa3d67072d0008eff3edfb23de89ebd9b6.txt, https://youtu.be/GOOtpiQ2Epo) - retail was already working off preliminary Q2 numbers two days before the scheduled print. The same digest also shows what the print is actually being asked to deliver instead of numbers ('it's monday and there's no buyout announcement', 'we need news this week', 'one of these days Cohen is gonna drop the bomb'), which is a high and non-financial bar.

findings.finding: GameStop raised capital twice in the four weeks before the print - 8-K items 1.01/3.02/8.01/9.01 accepted 2026-08-03T10:12:28Z and items 1.01/2.02/3.02/7.01/9.01 accepted 2026-08-31T06:23:08Z, both carrying item 3.02 unregistered sales of equity securities - while the stock sat within 7.2% of its 52-week low and 30.8% below its 52-week high.
findings.why_not_priced: Two item 3.02 events inside a month is a rate of issuance that does not show up in any summary of the name, and the second one was folded into the same 8-K as the preliminary results, so the financing and the numbers were reported as one story. The tape shows no distinct de-rating on either date, which is what I would expect to see if the dilution had been separately priced.
findings.independence: The StockTwits digest fetched 2026-08-30 independently frames the same risk from the holder side ('will he do another bond dilution for the rest of the 0% interest bonds', 2026-08-28) and reports a 14% rise in Robinhood's borrow rate for GME warrants on 2026-08-28 - a funding-cost signal on the same capital structure. This finding shares the 2026-08-31 8-K with my first finding and should be collapsed into that source cluster; only the 2026-08-03 8-K is genuinely additional.

what the eight 425 business-combination communications filed between 2026-06-24 and 2026-07-20 relate to: the StockTwits digests assert an attempt to acquire eBay and note that GameStop received over $13m of eBay dividends in the quarter, and separately anticipate 'the Delaware 251(g) filing', which together with the 8-K items 5.03/5.07 accepted 2026-07-08T10:33:19Z would suggest a holding-company reorganisation - but no filing body in this capture confirms any of it and I did not build a finding on it

the strike, size and expiry of the warrant tranche the digests keep returning to ('$1.8 billion cash injection', 'adjust the warrant strike price to 18.50', 'IF in October, warrants squeeze'): no filing body in the capture states any of those terms, so I cannot test whether an October expiry sits inside the reaction window

baseline_tension: It cuts against the run-in, which is +7.22% over five days, and it agrees with the baseline's own warning - the baseline scored this event 'suspect' on cadence and discounted the entire reaction history to zero usable events, so the 4.79% median it hands me is the number I am most confident is too large.
